author: First State Times
title: Railroad Commission of Texas Chairman Jim Wright elected to IOGCC leadership
text:
Jim Wright, Chairman of the Railroad Commission of Texas, was elected as Second Vice Chair of the Interstate Oil and Gas Compact Commission during its annual business meeting in Oklahoma City on May 20.
The appointment places Wright in a key leadership position within an organization that brings together governors from oil and gas producing states. The Interstate Oil and Gas Compact Commission includes 31 member states, seven affiliate states, select federal agencies, and representatives from seven Canadian provinces. The group works collectively to address challenges facing the industry while promoting responsible regulation and resource conservation.
Wright will succeed Jessie Chmielowski, Commissioner of the Alaska Oil and Gas Conservation Commission. As Second Vice Chair representing Texas at the IOGCC, he will focus on collaboration among member states. “It is a privilege to step into this leadership role at such a pivotal time for American energy,” emphasized Chairman Wright. “The IOGCC demonstrates that states are best positioned to regulate their natural resources effectively. As Second Vice Chair, my focus will be to foster collaboration among member states, share best practices and ensure our collective voice is heard on the national stage. Together, we will continue to support common-sense policies that drive economic growth, ensure energy security and protect public safety.”
Wright has served as Railroad Commissioner since his election in November 2020 and was unanimously chosen as Chairman in 2025. He is a lifelong South Texan with roots as a fifth-generation rancher.
He said he believes Texas’ economic future remains closely tied to its energy sector’s long-term strength and that access to global markets is crucial for maintaining its status as an economic leader.
The Railroad Commission of Texas regulates oil and gas operations across the state along with alternative fuels safety, natural gas utilities, surface mining activities, and intrastate pipelines. Established in 1891, it stands as Texas’ oldest regulatory agency.
